transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-03 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 mins
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Marquez (Redwood SE), Lena Patel (CISO, Argyll), Omar Khan (Platform Lead, Argyll), Mariana Ruiz (Compliance), Tom Ellis (Product)

Summary (auto): quick discovery re: where customer needs data to live, keystore options, and what evidence they need for audit.

[00:00] Sophie Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sophie from Redwood Inference, this is Diego our solutions engineer. Really looking forward to learning about your residency and compliance constraints.
[00:12] Lena Patel: Hi all. We'll probably jump in with our big ask up front — we need to make sure any inference paths for account creation stay within EU zones and keys are not exportable, also minimal logs.
[00:24] Diego Marquez: Got it, thanks Lena. Quick clarifying q — when you say "keys not exportable" do you mean KMS keys managed by you in your VPC HSM, or just that logs can't contain key material?
[00:38] Mariana Ruiz: Sorry, yeah, to be explicit — we need customer-managed KMS with key material never leaving our control. Our legal team calls it "key residency" and they specifically asked about hardware keystores and custody.
[00:50] Omar Khan: Also, we have a processing footprint: account origination flows will call the model for fraud scoring. Latency under 300ms is preferred, but we can't route traffic outside EU for that path.
[01:06] Sophie Chen: Makes sense. Two parts: hosting (where inference runs) and keystore (where keys live). Redwood offers Hosted (multi-tenant), Dedicated (reserved capacity in region), and Private (VPC/on-prem). For key residency you can use our Private/VPC option or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS integrations depending on your risk appetite.
[01:26] Tom Ellis: Quick — if we do Dedicated in eu-west-1, can we stop any telemetry from leaving the cluster? We need to know what logs Redwood captures by default.
[01:35] Diego Marquez: By default we capture request-level telemetry for billing and SLOs; that's token counts, latencies, and error traces. We do not store full prompt text in the hosted logs by default but there are exceptions for debugging unless redaction is enabled. However for Dedicated and Private we can configure log retention and redact PII at the agent level.
[01:54] Lena Patel: 'Agent level' — concrete example? We can't have raw customer PII in control plane logs ever.
[02:02] Diego Marquez: Understood. For Dedicated we have an opt-in setting to disable control-plane payload logging and an edge redaction hook that strips out pattern-matched fields before sending to central telemetry. It's something we set up in the tenancy config. There are a couple of caveats — service traces and sampling might still exist unless you request full disabling and a signed operational agreement.
[02:25] Mariana Ruiz: We need an attestation or something for that — our auditors will want to see the config entries and evidence. SOC2 is good but we need granular proof.
[02:34] Sophie Chen: Totally. We'll share our SOC2 Type II and a keystore + telemetry whitepaper. For more granular evidence, we can provide configuration templates and screenshots of the Dedicated tenancy settings, and if required, a JV-style runbook during a POC to demonstrate the redaction pipeline.
[02:52] Omar Khan: How does Redwood handle legal holds or e-discovery? If a regulator asks for records, what's your process?
[03:00] Diego Marquez: Good question. For Hosted customers we have a legal process that can pull tenant logs with proper notices, but for Dedicated/Private, logs are in customer-controlled storage options — you can choose S3 buckets in your account or our isolated storage with restricted access. We support legal hold flags that mark a request and increase retention.
[03:20] Lena Patel: So if we pick Dedicated with our own S3, does Redwood still have any copy? That would be a deal breaker.
[03:28] Sophie Chen: We can do Dedicated where the customer owns the S3 and we never mirror the logs to our central plane. In that config we only have operational telemetry in aggregated form. We also offer an option to disable debug dumps entirely.
[03:41] Tom Ellis: What about cross-border failover? We need fallback to a secondary region in case of outage, but failover must not move EU PII to non-EU soil.
[03:50] Diego Marquez: Right — routing policy can be region-locked. Redwood's smart routing supports hard region pins per route, and fallbacks can be configured to only use compatible regions. If you want strict non-export, we can disable cross-region fallback for that route. That will affect availability SLA though.
[04:08] Mariana Ruiz: Our compliance team won't accept any fallback that could export data. So either keep it single-region or provide a manual runbook for takeover.
[04:17] Sophie Chen: That's fine — many customers choose manual DR for regulated flows. We'll document the trade-offs for you.
[04:25] Omar Khan: Let's talk KMS specifics — can Redwood integrate with our Azure Key Vault / HSM?
[04:31] Diego Marquez: Yes, we have integrations with major cloud KMS: GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault via managed HSM, and customers can bring their own key via external key management protocols. For Private deployments we can also support HSM direct attachments. We'll need to validate the crypto policy and TLS tunnel setup during the POC.
[04:50] Lena Patel: What about key escrow? Our legal ops wants to know about emergency access by Redwood — we do not want any backdoor or ability for Redwood to unwrap keys.
[04:59] Sophie Chen: No backdoors. For Dedicated where you provide KMS, Redwood services run with envelope encryption but we never store the unwrapped key. For Hosted, we provide a managed KMS option where keys are managed by us, but customers with high compliance needs tend to avoid that for sensitive flows.
[05:15] Tom Ellis: Can you explain envelope flow end-to-end? I'm trying to map it to our infra diagram.
[05:20] Diego Marquez: Sure — client encrypts or requests encryption of payloads, Redwood runtime uses a data-encryption-key (DEK) generated per-tenancy, the DEK is wrapped with your KMS key. The runtime only receives the wrapped key and never has access to the raw master key. For HSM-backed Private setups, you can require a call to your HSM for unwrap and we route those calls inside your VPC.
[05:43] Mariana Ruiz: Are there any telemetry side-channels? Even if you redact PII there can be model prompts with unique identifiers.
[05:51] Diego Marquez: Yes, good point. We recommend a two-step approach: client-side tokenization/ID hashing plus server-side redaction rules. We can also provide a pre-flight sanitizer you run before sending.
[06:04] Lena Patel: Our legal team also wants log minimization — what default retention windows are we talking about?
[06:10] Sophie Chen: Default telemetry retention is 90 days but for Dedicated/Private you can set as low as 7 days or indefinite depending on your bucket policy. We can also set immutable retention for legal holds.
[06:22] Omar Khan: Cost — Dedicated with customer KMS and private storage, how much heavier is that versus Hosted? Ballpark numbers now are fine.
[06:30] Sophie Chen: Roughly Dedicated is 2.5–3x hosted per-token cost if you're reserving capacity due to reserved GPU costs and private storage. Private/VPC with HSM and egress controls adds infra and ops fees; we'll include a sample TCO in the POC doc.
[06:44] Tom Ellis: I want to lock down sample success criteria — what would we need to see in the POC to move forward?
[06:50] Sophie Chen: From our side a clear set: 1) demonstrate keystore integration with your Azure HSM, 2) show log redaction removing identified PII patterns, 3) run 1000-sample latency/throughput benchmark under your expected payloads hitting <300ms p95, and 4) provide the evidence artifacts for your auditors (config screenshots + runbook).
[07:12] Mariana Ruiz: Also add legal hold behavior: show that a hold request marks the streams and retention is extended and that we can export a preserved set.
[07:21] Diego Marquez: We'll bring a POC plan with a schedule and gates.
[07:25] Sophie Chen: Quick note — one caveat is model variants. If you use quantized variants for cost we need to ensure no change in PII handling — runtime behavior is equivalent but we'll add tests.
[07:36] Lena Patel: Are there any known regulatory red flags with Redwood's telemetry architecture? Anything auditors usually bring up?
[07:44] Sophie Chen: Most auditors ask for: where logs live, who can access them, KMS ownership, and evidence of redaction. We supply that, plus we can run a joint session with our security engineer to walk your auditors.
[07:58] Omar Khan: On timeline — we want a POC in Q4, ideally kickoff in mid-October. Is that feasible?
[08:04] Diego Marquez: Yes, mid-Oct kickoff is feasible. We'll need contract sign-off for Dedicated capacity and a small engineering timebox for integration.
[08:13] Tom Ellis: For the POC can we get a temporary tenancy in eu-west-1 with the same config as production?
[08:20] Sophie Chen: Yes, sandbox Dedicated tenancy mirrors the prod config. We'll scope it in the POC proposal.
[08:26] Mariana Ruiz: A couple of quick questions I forgot to ask — SOC2 scoping, do you support HIPAA/BAA? We have partners handling health-adjacent data occasionally.
[08:36] Sophie Chen: Redwood currently has SOC2 Type II. We support HIPAA use cases under a BAA for Private deployments — Hosted is a case-by-case. We can attach BAA for Dedicated/Private with required controls.
[08:50] Lena Patel: Ok that helps.
[08:53] Diego Marquez: Also, small note — for e-discovery we can produce lineage logs but you should expect them to be at sampling granularity unless we run full capture which you control in Dedicated.
[09:04] Tom Ellis: Great. Anything else?
[09:07] Mariana Ruiz: One last — does Redwood offer key escrow or emergency unlocking if we lose keys? We want to avoid third-party escrow but need an operational option.
[09:17] Sophie Chen: We don't provide unsolicited escrow. We can enable a customer-controlled split-key escrow that you manage — for example, multi-party escrow where you hold one share and we hold another but can't reconstruct alone. That's an optional add-on and we'd document it.
[09:31] Omar Khan: That could work.
[09:33] Sophie Chen: Okay we'll capture action items — we'll send SOC2 and keystore whitepaper, Diego will schedule the benchmark, Mariana will share sanitized logs.
[09:44] Tom Ellis: Thanks everyone.
[09:46] Lena Patel: Thanks. That was helpful.
[09:48] Meeting end.
